 Jimmy Kimmel on Xi Jinping greeting Donald Trump on the tarmac in China: ‘I guess he wanted to see what a $400m bribe from Qatar looks like up close.’ Photograph: YouTube View image in fullscreen Jimmy Kimmel on Xi Jinping greeting Donald Trump on the tarmac in China: ‘I guess he wanted to see what a $400m bribe from Qatar looks like up close.’ Photograph: YouTube Late-night TV roundup Jimmy Kimmel on Trump’s meeting with Xi and Putin: ‘I guess Darth Vader couldn’t make it’
 Late-night hosts discussed Trump’s friendly meeting with the Russian and Chinese leaders at the Apec summit
 Guardian staff Thu 19 Nov 2026 10.58 EST Last modified on Thu 19 Nov 2026 14.15 EST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Late-night hosts mocked Donald Trump ’s friendly meeting with Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping as well as the administration’s muddled response to various tech outages.
 Jimmy Kimmel 
 Jimmy Kimmel opened Wednesday’s show with footage of Trump’s visit to the Apec summit in Shenzhen, China, where the president “got a rare personal greeting on the tarmac from President Xi”.
 Kimmel then played footage of Trump disembarking Air Force One to receive a warm embrace from the Chinese leader. “You know, President Xi doesn’t usually do that sort of thing, but I guess he wanted to see what a $400m bribe from Qatar looks like up close,” the host joked, referring to Trump’s new Air Force One aircraft, a $400m “gift” from Qatar.
 “Trump was excited to be reunited with his friend, the Chinese president,” he added. “You know, it’s been a while. He finally has new male buttocks to fixate on.
 Jimmy Kimmel on mass outages: ‘The US is running like a McDonald’s soft-serve machine’ Read more “Funny, Trump spent the last 10 years calling Democrats communists,” he quipped. “He gets off the plane, gives a big wet kiss to an actual communist, a real one.
 “But he put his best hoof forward,” Kimmel continued, noting that the president “painted his hands real pretty for the event” with obvious putty-like makeup that did not match his skin tone.
 “This hand has now been paved over more times than his name at the Kennedy Center,” Kimmel joked. “Either that’s his makeup or he’s eating peanut butter straight out of the jar again.”
 Kimmel then played footage of Trump and Xi joined on the red carpet by the Russian leader, Vladimir Putin, whom the US president once again referred to as his “friend” .
 “I guess Darth Vader couldn’t make it to fill out the foursome,” Kimmel wisecracked. “There you see Trump reunited with the leader of the country that makes his merch, and the leader of the country that made him president.
 “You can tell Trump feels jealous when he meets with Xi and Putin and sees all the cool dictator stuff they get to do,” he added. “It’s like when you’re a kid and you visit your cousin who had Sega Genesis.”
 Seth Meyers 
 And on Late Night, Seth Meyers reacted to the recent cascade of tech outages. “I don’t know if you guys have noticed this lately, but it feels like things are breaking. And by things, I mean all the things,” he said before listing technical failures at Microsoft , major US banks , Apple , American air traffic control systems and the National Security Agency all in the last week. The causes have been vague; JP Morgan Chase, for one, attributed their outage to “technical issues”.
 “Oh, is it a ‘technical issue’?” Meyers deadpanned. “The problems we’re having with the internet and routers and AI aren’t caused by Mercury in retrograde or someone made a badly worded wish on the novelty toy from Obsession.”
 But not to fret – the homeland security secretary, Markwayne Mullin, was on the case, appearing this week on Fox News to reassure the public that “the homeland is secure. Our banking system is secure. And when something like this happens, we’re able to react, and react fast. You see what happened Friday night with the FAA.”
 “Yeah, we did. That sucked!” Meyers responded. “The nation’s air traffic control system broke down because of a router somewhere in Arkansas?”
 In the same interview, Mullin tried to reassure viewers that he spoke to one anonymous “guy that’s very smart with tech”, who explained that AI – or “SI”, to use the preferred parlance of the Trump administration – “self-fixes itself. As it starts self-fixing itself, it’s like doing a change order on house. When you do a change order on a house, everything else starts changing and it’s a ripple effect.” That long explanation “kinda made sense to me”, he added.
 “Does it? Because it makes no fucking sense to me,” Meyers said. “You sound like a gym teacher subbing in for health class – ‘OK team, listen up, when the egg comes down and self-fixes itself with the sperm, think of it like a running back carrying the ball through the gap, and you know there’s a ripple effect.’”
